subject: Halcyon4B elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer update, mitigations, and next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: BrightBox ProdOps <prodops@brightbox.ai>, Sasha Cole <sasha.cole@brightbox.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22 09:12 -0800
Subject: Halcyon4B — elevated 5xx/timeouts observed (initial notice)

Sasha / BrightBox team,

Quick update from Redwood: starting ~08:40 PST we observed an uptick in 5xx errors and request timeouts for requests routed to model halcyon4b (production variant halcyon4b-v2). The spike is concentrated on inference flows that use long context windows (>6k tokens) and high concurrency. We've attached a short metrics snapshot (halcyon4b-metrics-20261122.png).

What we’ve done so far:
- Automatically routed new requests to a compatibility fallback (halcyon4b-compat / halcyon3b-compat) for eligible traffic to preserve latency SLOs.
- Throttled a small fraction of high-concurrency requests and temporarily increased autoscale by 25% to burn down queued tokens.
- Isolated a small set of GPU instances suspected to be running the recent kernel build that shipped in the last runtime release. Those instances have been taken out of the rotation.

Immediate ask from you: please reply if you continue to see errors on your side and include one representative request id (or attach a short server-side log snippet). That will help us correlate with our traces quickly.

Owners/next steps (internal): Marcus will lead the kernel rollback and recompile; Neha will validate KV cache behavior under long contexts; Jonas will coordinate rollout policy and routing config. I’ll keep you posted with a recovery ETA within the next 90 minutes.

Sorry for the interruption — we’ll prioritize a fast, clear fix and follow up with a postmortem.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Halcyon4B — elevated 5xx/timeouts observed (initial notice)

Thanks Priyom — we are seeing the same failures on our end. Error pattern: a lot of 502s and occasional 504s, mainly from our summarization pipeline with long prior context. Attached is a short snippet from our side (brightbox-error-sample-logs.txt).

Two customer-impact notes:
- Some batch jobs are retrying aggressively, which is increasing queued requests; we’ve paused those for now.
- We’re seeing a 10-12% increase in user-facing request latency for requests that fall back to halcyon3b compatibility mode.

Any estimate on when you expect normal behavior? We’d also like to request a short post-incident call once you have the RCA so we can plan an SDK-level mitigation.

—Sasha
Sasha Cole
ProdOps Lead | BrightBox AI
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBox ProdOps <prodops@brightbox.ai>, Sasha Cole <sasha.cole@brightbox.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22 10:01 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon4B — elevated 5xx/timeouts observed (initial notice)

Status update / technical summary (quick):
- Root cause hypothesis: a recent runtime kernel shader change (kernel v2.17.3) introduced a regression in KV cache addressing for long-context sequences on Ampere A100 hosts. Under certain concurrency patterns the KV retrieval path returned invalid offsets, which caused downstream decoder stalls and ultimately request timeouts and 502s.
- Evidence: trace sampling shows increased decode latency followed by RPC cancellations originating in the token emission loop. The attached metrics image shows a sharp spike in decode p95 correlated with the 5xx surge.

Actions taken (done):
1) Removed the nodes running kernel v2.17.3 from the pool and replaced them with nodes running kernel v2.16.9 (rollback).
2) Enabled routing fallback for long-context traffic to halcyon3b-compat for traffic that tolerates model degradation (already in effect).
3) Applied a temporary KV-cache warmup for pinned hot prefixes on the replaced nodes.

Planned next steps (timeline):
- 10:15 PST: complete rollback across all affected AZs (in progress).
- 10:45 PST: run a targeted randomized traffic replay for long-context flows to validate no residual 5xxs.
- 11:30 PST: begin a controlled recompile of v2.17.3 with an extra bounds-check patch; this will be staged in canary only.

Owners: Marcus (rollback + compile), Neha (end-to-end validation and perf regressions), Jonas (routing rules + customer comms). Priyom will lead customer liaison.

I’ll post results from the replay as soon as it completes.

—Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Attachment: halcyon4b-mitigation-runbook-v1.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Cole <sasha.cole@brightbox.ai>, BrightBox ProdOps <prodops@brightbox.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22 11:38 -0800
Subject: Halcyon4B — recovery confirmation and next steps

Sasha / BrightBox team,

Follow-up: rollback completed across the affected AZs at ~10:20 PST and the randomized replay finished at 10:50 PST with no elevated 5xxs observed in the replay window. Current metrics show error rates have returned to baseline for halcyon4b traffic and long-context requests are being routed normally. Attached is the mitigation runbook and the metric snapshot we referred to earlier.

Customer-facing summary of what happened:
- What happened: a kernel regression affecting KV cache addressing on long-context workloads caused increased decode latency and downstream 502/504 errors for halcyon4b-v2.
- Impact: BrightBox experienced a ~10% latency uplift for a short window and a spike in 5xxs; we routed eligible traffic to a compatibility fallback to maintain availability.
- What we did: removed affected nodes, rolled back kernel to v2.16.9, warmed caches, increased autoscale briefly, and validated with randomized replays.
- Short-term mitigation: we will continue to keep a canary of the patched kernel in a small pool for 48 hours before a full re-rollout; we’ll also add stricter bounds-checking and an end-to-end long-context test in the preflight.

Next steps / commitments:
- Postmortem draft: we’ll share a full RCA (including timeline, logs, and test artifacts) by 2026-11-25 EOD.
- Follow-up call: available windows on 2026-11-24 between 09:00–11:00 PST; let us know what works.
- Credits: per our incident policy we’ll evaluate a one-time service credit given the customer impact; details will be shared in the postmortem.

Please reply if you still see issues or want this escalated to an executive sync. Thank you for the quick coordination.

—Priyom
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear runbook. We confirm errors have subsided on our side and the customer tickets have quieted down. 11/24 09:00 PST works for a follow-up.

A couple of asks for the postmortem: please include the small dataset we used for long-context repro (we’ll attach it to the HubSpot ticket) and any recommended SDK-level backoff guidance to avoid aggressive client retries for future transient errors.

Looking forward to the RCA and the credit details.

—Sasha
